 Welcome to the Frost Mage rotation guide for ! This guide will teach you all about the optimal rotation for Frost Mage across its various talent builds. It will cover both core ability cadence and cooldown usage in dungeons and raids for .

Basics

Frost Mage Rotation in 

Frost Mage is a relatively straightforward specialization in Midnight. While there are nuances to learn, the rotation is mainly based on consuming stacks of a debuff on your targets, keeping cooldowns running, and reacting to some random procs.

 

 

 
 Utilize Shatter: Avoid wasting stacks of the Freezing debuff. You can consume them and trigger Shatter with some spells like Ice Lance and Comet Storm .
 

 

 
 

 
 Utilize your Major Cooldowns: Ray of Frost and Frozen Orb deal a lot of damage and should be used often.
 

 

 
 

 
 Use Procs and Minor Cooldowns: Spells like Flurry and Glacial Spike are powerful and you'll want to use them often. In AoE, this also includes Blizzard . You will sometimes get procs like Fingers of Frost or Brain Freeze that you'll typically want to spend quickly. 
 

 

 
 

 
 Always be Casting: It's important to always be doing something. Even if the spells you are casting are suboptimal, doing so is significantly better than casting nothing while trying to decide what to do. Frostbolt / Frostfire Bolt is the main filler spell here for Frost Mage and Ice Lance can be used while moving. 
 

 

Frost Mage Starter Guide

 Best Frost Mage Rotation

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Frost Mage: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.

 Frost Mage in Single Target plays around a priority list, juggling both ability cooldowns and resources. As every cast and GCD finishes, you can simply follow this list from top to bottom and press the button with the current highest value. If you press a spell just before the previous cast or GCD ends, it will be queued immediately after the prior spell.

 This is also a good rotation to use against 2 targets.

Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Frost Mage to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content. While consumables like flasks and food make a big difference, you can skip them in content that you do not need the extra power for.

 Frost Mage Major Cooldowns

Frost's major cooldowns are quite a bit different with the rework in Midnight. Ray of Frost does a ton of damage and helps to speed up the rotation, but also leaves you quite vulnerable while you are using it.

 
 Ray of Frost 

 Ray of Frost is the major cooldown for Frost Mage. It deals a lot of damage and generates a lot of Freezing stacks. The most important thing to remember here is making sure that you can get the full channel off. Be ready to Shimmer to safety instead of canceling it and plan ahead if necessary to make sure you use it at a safe time.

 When playing ]Frostfire with multiple targets, you can prioritize spending Frostfire Empowerment first so that Comet Storm has more Freezing stacks to consume when you use it.

 
 Comet Storm 

 Comet Storm replaces Ray of Frost after you cast it. Keep in mind that in AoE situations this can Shatter stacks on multiple targets at once.

 
 Time Warp 

 Use Time Warp before Ray of Frost or when your group needs it. This is an extremely powerful cooldown, but you can typically only use it once per boss fight and rarely in dungeons and the open world.

 Frost Mage Advanced Tips

While the Frost rotation is relatively simple, it is important to keep in mind how the class interacts with encounters and take that into account to optimize your performance.

 
 Charged Cooldowns 

 Frost Mage has a big advantage over the other Mage specializations in Midnight, which is the charged cooldowns gained by Hand of Frost and Glacial Bulwark .
 
With Hand of Frost at level 90, Ray of Frost will have 2 charges, which provides significant flexibility in when you do deal damage. Keep it on cooldown, but as long as you have less than two charges you have a lot of choice in when you use the other charge. In particular, this has the potential to be very strong when bosses have vulnerability phases or spawn priority adds that must be killed.

 Glacial Bulwark grants two charges of both Ice Barrier and Ice Block / Ice Cold . This makes it much easier to ensure that you have defensive cooldowns available for big damage events and offers a huge optimization opportunity if you're interesting in carefully scripting out all of your defensive usages in a boss fight.
 

Our Frost Mage guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on View Changelog in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Frost Mage guides for , make sure to browse the Navigation Bar at the top of the page, along with our list of Related Guides just beneath the Table of Contents .

Notes will appear here.
Because Thermal Void is very impactful, you should use it before getting a new one from using Brain Freeze.
This is minor against one target, but it is significant when cleaving an extra target to prioritize this and avoid wasting Fingers of Frost.
Be sure you are using Ray of Frost early in your opener. Also use it at high priority at the end of the fight or during important burst moments if it's available.
You can elect not to use Blizzard here if its cooldown won't be ready before Frozen Orb's cooldown finishes. This allows you to use it with Freezing Rain immediately after Frozen Orb.
If you have 5 Icicles, opening with Glacial Spike is ideal, but due to the 12.0.5 changes you can't always do this, especially because pulling a raid boss will reset your Icicles.

In the priority list, AE is last only to Frostbolt, this also suggests this is a cleave priority list.

What further confuses me, the first thing you do under Multitarget is point out that cleave follows single target rotation and just to take Splitting Ice. This suggests that the multitarget priority list should be for AoE. Having it be for AoE also keeps the flow of the guide from ST, to Cleave, to AoE(Opposed to ST, to Cleave, to AoE, back to Cleave). Since there is no mention of AoE priority other than Blizzard and Arcane Explosion, it is missing talent priority, Frost Orb, CoC, and what to do once you're out of mana. That also makes it likely for the priority list to be for AoE. But because of reasons already stated, it doesn't make sense for it to be AoE, or a hybrid of Cleave and AoE.

I have no idea what this priority list was designed for.If it's for both Cleave and AoE; it doesn't follow AoE logistics. If it's for Cleave; the guide already sort of says it's redundant and there's a lot of missing information regarding AoE. Regardless, the bit stating to use Blizzard and AE in AoE situations above all else isn't as helpful as it could be when a large and bold priority list that does not have "Cleave" or any specifications anywhere near it, says otherwise. It makes your guide contradict itself. 

In my opinion - Cleave and AoE should be separated rather than a catch-all "Multitarget" while only providing a priority list for what realistically is only Cleave. This could add a differential on spells moving up in priority for different numbers of targets. If you decide to keep it as is(Under one header), please move the AoE selection below the Cleave priority so it flows from ST, to Cleave, then to AoE in a growing fashion and greatly expand on the AoE section.

Max Chain Reaction IL loses to CoC without shatter at 5-6 targets depending on critical strike chance.

2) The Shifting Power mention stating to only use if more than 3 targets is in the single target section - put this in the Multitarget section. In the ST section, I'd replace this with a mention saying to only use if you're targetless due to an intermission.

Comment by SyrusRex 
I'm seeing that much of this guidance is 2 years old and it's possible that this requires updating. I don't know if my rotation is the best one out there, but pulled 12.5k dps on the last Anduin kill we had and this is how I prioritize my rotating spells. Don't always bust your cds at the start--it depends on the fight, in the first part of Tierna Synthe (for example), you do a normal rotation till you knock the tree out of mind control--then you pop everything on the boss.

So I (necrolord) open for max dps in this order: icy veins, timewarp, deathborne, int potion--start spamming frostbolt. I don't have any "use" trinkets; I have unbound changeling and infinitely divisible ooze.

while you're frostbolting:

1. On FoF proc: insta ice lance on fingers of frost--you don't want to lose those, you can only have 2 at a time max, and they will re-proc and refresh--whether or not you use them, and that means you lost dps from an icelance crit you didn't cast.

2. Brain Freeze sub-rotation: When you get a brain freeze: cast a frostbolt, then mash flurry--the first bb from flury will beat the frostbolt in flight on the way to the target and debuff the target with "frozen" so your frostbolt will crit every time, then subsequent bbs all refresh the frozen debuff back to 2. So you frostbolt, flurry, icelance, icelance, and everything crits. If you are the perfect distance, you can frostbolt, flury, and icelance (which moves slower than flury, so you can't do this at max range, but if youre the right distance you can land an icelance before the last bb from flurry hits, so you can get a frostbolt, flurry, and 3x icelance crits from one brain freeze proc.
 --Try to don't cast brainfreeze when you have FoF proc'd: all that will do is eat both a frozen debuff and the FoF proc with the same icelance. try to empty the FoF procs before the Brain Freeze sub-rotatoin.

3. Frostbolt spam.

Pro-Tips:

for key aoe. I have a macro that centers a blizzard on me and frozen orb stops the minute it hits something, so if you throw a frozen orb from a distance at a pack you want to aoe, it only really tics on the one or two that are close to you. I walk up to the pac where the melee dps are, and hit icy veins which drops my rune, i cast blizzard, cast frozen orb right in the middle, frost nova, cone of cold, then spam frostbolts. Icy propulsion conduit ticks almost a second off the cd for crits, and icy propulsion extends icy veins when you get a crit against a frozen target, so all those tics and crits mean that you're going to pretty much have 100% uptime for icyveins during aoe if you do it right. you can do this really efficiently with the frozen orb talent because it makes your blizzard instant cast, and if you pay attention, you can actually get 2 instant cast blizzards off of one frozen orb if you hit blizzard right away after the first one finishes. that's if you want to be great at aoe damage--i think its better to be good at aoe and great at boss killing; frost mages have a great automatic 2/3 target cleave with splitting ice and deathborne-frostbolts (you spit out up to 3 frostbolts per cast--that's what I take). I don't take the 20% more procs because if you check your Details!, you'll see that your procs actually refresh before you can use them, more than 20% anyway, so if you're doing your rotation right, that's just a waste of a talent imo.

But the key to key aoe dps is always throwing that blizzard/frost orb/nova/coneofcold out, not really for the damage (but it's not bad damage), but you really do it to make sure that you are propelling your icy veins.
--I learned this because i was doing a key with a mage that I totally outgeared--my gear wrecked his, but he smoked my dps; I did 10k, he did 14k. I figured out he did it by casting blizzard all the time--the damage wasn't from blizzard though. His icy veins uptime was 60% of the whole key--mine was 20%, that's how he out played me--all the little crits kept his icy veins up 3x more than me which is how he out damaged me.

stop stacking crit at 33.3% (that's all you need to guarantee crits against frozen targets)--you can actually get away with less than that though because there's always food and raid buffs that give you more crit so you don't actually need to go all the way to 33.3. 31 or 32 is probably more than enough. I'm going to try 30 and see what happens.

stop stacking haste at 30% because when you hero+icy veins+legendary and all the haste buffs you get, you will cast frostbolt faster than the global cooldown--it rips. You'll be tempted to just spam frostbolt because it's pretty badass to rip 3 frostbolts at a time faster than a 1 sec cast so, as necrolord when you go skele with maximum cd's popped, you have 3 waves of 3 frostbolts flying through the air at max range, and damage hammering--I've routinely bursted at 35k dps for 20 seconds with everything popped.

Then it's all versatility for the straight damage increase--when i run simulators mastery is always below versatility. It's not horrible, but get your crit close to capped, cap your haste at a tiny bit more than 30%, then all versatility.

One more thing blink to move when you can--go to the trainer and get the blink where you blink the direction you move, not straight forward. so strafe quick in the direction you want to go, blink and keep casting. If you know you're going to need to run because stuff on the ground is going to appear or something, then try to store up 2 FoF procs and a BF proc, so that will let you move, and still be throwing out big damage for at least 6 seconds, when you strafe to move while facing the boss, you can throw icelance, icelance (eating your FoF procs), flurry (eating the BF proc), and then icelance, icelance, which will crit against the frozen target--so when you move for 6 seconds, you're still going to be doing insane damage. If you take ice floes, then you can rip some frostbolts on the move too--but that's too hardcore for me.

This rotation will make you a very competent mage-dps'r. If you can master keeping your icy veins up-time really high (with the rotation and all the baby crits from blizzards and cold orbs) then you will post astounding dps as a frost mage.

This is the rotation/priority that I think works well for me.

For the Alliance!
-Syrus
